name: Precision Bench
description: The product on a lapped black granite surface plate, ringed by anodised aluminium and tool-steel measuring gear squared to it on a strict orthogonal grid, under calibration-grade even light. Engineering precision used as art direction — the alignment is the composition.
lighting: Calibration-grade even light, one specular per chamfer
subject: product
prompt: the subject is the hero of the frame and occupies roughly 55 percent of the frame width, tack-sharp and clearly lit, set on a lapped black granite surface plate whose top reads as a dead-flat non-reflective charcoal field with a fine stippled lapping texture and one chamfered edge catching a thin bright line, every object on the plate mutually square, each item's edges parallel or perpendicular to every other item's edges on one shared orthogonal grid at deliberate equal engineering spacing, nothing rotated off that grid by even a few degrees, three steel gauge blocks wrung into one solid column with their lapped faces in full contact so the joins read as hairline dark lines only, with no gap, step or daylight between the blocks, a hard-anodised sine bar in deep blue with a precision cylindrical roll pinned at each end, a red-anodised parallel clamp, a dial indicator on a chrome column stand whose face is left completely blank, plain white with no numerals, graduation marks, lettering or printed scale of any kind, its plunger lowered onto the subject so the contact tip physically touches the top face with no gap, calibration-grade even lighting from one very large source directly overhead plus two low fill cards so the scene carries almost no shadow gradient and the object edges do all the separating, exactly one controlled specular streak running the length of each machined chamfer and nowhere else, shadows short crisp and honest directly beneath each object with true contact, deep focus holding the whole layout crisp corner to corner, colour held to charcoal granite, tool-steel grey and satin black with the anodised blue and red as the only saturation, real anodised finish showing a fine directional brush under the dye rather than painted plastic, genuine lapped-granite matte that refuses to mirror, no workshop clutter, no swarf oil or coolant, no printed callouts, dimension lines, rulers or measurement graphics, no numerals, digits or graduated scales on any instrument face, bezel or stand, no glowing screens or indicator lights, no coloured gel light, no second product, immaculate technical commercial clarity
